## Design

### 2026-10-13 – Today was a shorter work session than I hoped, but I did get most of the Starbie case done!

**0.78h**

Today was a shorter work session than I hoped, but I did get most of the Starbie case done!

I started off by exporting my PCB from KiCad and importing it into Onshape.

![Screenshot 2026-10-13 212128](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/sE7vZfeaqmfwXllHYiqPgB7QRPGwMqyP/17521cbe52027f402b98d37b8962cd9ea6581a9682c0d524c45ce6c4316407a0.png)

I used this both to copy the outline of the PCB for a snug fit and to figure out how thick I would need my enclosure to be to fit all my components. I'm fairly sure my DHT11 will be the tallest component on my PCB. I think I'll put it on the bottom of my PCB; if they're on the same side I'll either have a stupid sensor sticking out of my enclosure or you'll have to reach an inch into the enclosure to hit the Starbie's buttons.

I messed around with the dimensions a bit, then I added some nice fillets and added a keychain hole.

![Screenshot 2026-10-13 212059](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/sE7vZfeaqmfwXllHYiqPgB7QRPGwMqyP/dd5c7ad8985e62f51b23982a5bdbc36c877f3dc77139eeecc410b02837b05f4e.png)

This was my stopping point for the day. Tomorrow I'm going to add some tabs to keep the PCB vertically in place and add a screen cutout.
